---
title: "Choosing an atlas"
---

`iblatlas` offers four atlases, but they are not four independent volumes. Three of them are
the Allen CCF with different linear scalings applied, and one is a genuinely different
parcellation.

## The four

| Atlas | What it is | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `AllenAtlas` | The Allen CCF, unscaled | 10, 25 or 50 µm (default 25) |
| `NeedlesAtlas` | Allen CCF, scaled from the Dorr 2008 MRI atlas | as Allen |
| `MRITorontoAtlas` | Allen CCF, scaled from the Qiu 2018 MRI atlas | as Allen |
| `FranklinPaxinosAtlas` | Franklin–Paxinos, matched to the CCF by Chon et al. | (10, 100, 10) µm |

Start with `AllenAtlas` unless you have a specific reason not to. The annotations IBL uses are
the 2017 (CCFv2) version.

::: {.callout-warning}
## `NeedlesAtlas` and `MRITorontoAtlas` are functions, not classes

Both are factory functions that return a scaled `AllenAtlas`. They are not subclasses, so an
`isinstance` check against them does not merely return `False` — it raises:

```python
isinstance(ba, NeedlesAtlas)
# TypeError: isinstance() arg 2 must be a type, a tuple of types, or a union
```

Test with `isinstance(ba, AllenAtlas)` and inspect the scaling if you need to tell them apart.
:::

## The two MRI scalings, and in vivo versus ex vivo

This is the distinction people ask about most, partly because the literature and the code use
different names for the same things. "Qiu 2018" is `MRITorontoAtlas`. "Dorr 2008" and "DSURQE"
are `NeedlesAtlas`.

| | Source | Acquisition | Subjects | ML | AP | DV |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NeedlesAtlas` | Dorr 2008 DSURQE | post-mortem, brain in skull | 40 C57BL/6J, p84 | 1 | 1.087 | 0.952 |
| `MRITorontoAtlas` | Qiu 2018 | ***in vivo*** | 12, p65 | 0.952 | 1.031 | 0.885 |

Four things follow from that table.

**Both are scalings on one volume.** Neither is a separate image or a separate label set. The
region boundaries and the region ids are identical to the Allen CCF; only the mapping from
coordinates to voxels changes. Switching atlas does not change what a region *is*.

**There is no in vivo / ex vivo switch.** You cannot ask the package for "the in vivo version"
of an atlas. The distinction is a property of how each source MRI was acquired, which is then
baked into that atlas's three scaling factors — and nothing else. Needles was imaged
post-mortem with the brain still inside the skull; Qiu 2018 imaged living animals.

**They disagree, most of all in depth.** The DV factors are 0.952 and 0.885 — roughly a 7%
difference in predicted depth. At 4 mm that is about 270 µm, which is more than enough to put
a probe tip in the wrong structure. The ML factors differ too: Needles applies none at all.

**The Allen CCF is neither.** With scaling `(1, 1, 1)` it is not an in vivo frame, nor the
ex vivo MRI frame — it is a serial two-photon average of fixed, extracted tissue, with its own
distortions.

::: {.callout-important}
## Which scaling to use for in vivo targeting is an open question

The package expresses no preference and neither docstring advises one. The acquisition argues
for `MRITorontoAtlas`, since it was imaged in living animals. IBL practice, and the fact that
the default atlas cache path is `histology/ATLAS/Needles/Allen`, point towards `NeedlesAtlas`.

This documentation deliberately does not recommend one. Ask an experimentalist in your group
what your lab uses, and record the answer with your coordinates.
:::

## Franklin–Paxinos is the different one

`FranklinPaxinosAtlas` is a different parcellation, not a scaled CCF — the Mouse Brain in
Stereotaxic Coordinates, 4th edition, matched onto the CCF by Chon et al. Its resolution is
anisotropic: 10 µm in ML and DV, but **100 µm in AP**. If you are slicing coronally and the
result looks coarse, that is why.

It also has its own bregma landmark, distinct from the Allen one.

## Relationship to planning tools

[Pinpoint](https://virtualbrainlab.org/pinpoint/in_vivo_alignment.html) is the tool many IBL
users plan in vivo trajectories with. It offers CCF, Qiu 2018, Dorr 2008 and a legacy IBL Dorr
transform, and it applies a −5° pitch correction that `iblatlas` does not
(see [Coordinates and volumes](coordinates-and-volumes.qmd)).

Those names overlap with the ones above, but **it has not been confirmed that the transforms
are the same**. Do not assume an `Insertion` and a Pinpoint plan are expressed in the same
frame without checking. State which tool produced a coordinate when you record it.
